memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The angel of the Lord found Hagar near a spring in the desert; it was the spring that is beside the road to Shur. And he said, "Hagar, slave of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?" - Gen 16:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Hagar has run away - a pregnant slave with no plan, no protector, heading back toward Egypt through the desert. And God comes looking for her. "The angel of the Lord found Hagar." She wasn't seeking Him. She was simply fleeing her pain. But God sought her out and found her by a spring in the wilderness.

Consider who this is. Hagar is nobody by the world's reckoning - a foreign slave woman, used and discarded, running away. And she becomes the first person in all of Scripture to be personally sought out and addressed by the angel of the Lord. Not Abram the patriarch. A runaway slave. God's heart runs toward the overlooked.

And notice the tenderness of His question: "Hagar" - He calls her by name. "Where have you come from, and where are you going?" He isn't gathering information; He knows already. He's inviting her to pour out her story, to be seen and heard. This is a God who meets the broken not with accusation but with gentle questions.

This is the God we worship - the One who "came to seek and to save the lost" (Luke 19:10), the Shepherd who leaves the flock to find the one wandering sheep (Luke 15:4). You may feel you have run too far, that no one is looking for you. But God pursues His people into the wilderness. He knows your name, and He is seeking you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you felt too far gone for God to come after you?
- Do you believe God pursues the overlooked and the runaway?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You pursue me into the wilderness, calling me by name. When I run, come and find me. Thank You that You seek the lost and the overlooked, and that You see me.
Amen.
